claims.text: Adding mass-fluctuation and local-force-constant descriptors to a data-driven model will improve identification of HEAs with ultra-low phonon thermal conductivity.
Conventional predictive models rely on averaged structural properties or general phase descriptors without explicitly representing local chemical disorder.
FeCoCrMnNi is representative of single-phase, random-solid-solution HEAs with a disordered crystalline structure.
Disorder-specific descriptors, including mass fluctuation and force-constant variability, can be computed or extracted from alloy composition data for model-based screening.
Strong chemical disorder in HEAs produces local atomic-mass and force-constant fluctuations.
Mass and force-constant fluctuations enhance phonon scattering and reduce phonon lifetimes.
Mass and force-constant fluctuations disrupt long-wavelength phonon propagation.
Reduced phonon lifetimes lower lattice thermal conductivity.
Phonon-scattering sources introduced through entropy engineering can produce very low lattice thermal conductivity.
Representing disorder effects will produce a closer predictive relationship between composition and thermal behavior.
The disorder-aware model will identify HEAs whose measured phonon thermal conductivity is approximately 20% lower, or statistically significantly lower, than values predicted by conventional models.
The approach is mainly applicable to single-phase HEAs in a random-solid-solution state.
Phase segregation, nanocrystallization, or composite microstructures can introduce additional scattering mechanisms that limit the reliability of a disorder-descriptor model.
Oxidation and nanocrystalline grain boundaries can alter phonon scattering and confound the proposed comparison.
Failure of model-selected HEAs to exhibit a statistically significant or at least 20% thermal-conductivity reduction relative to conventionally selected HEAs would falsify the hypothesis.
